BILL NUMBER:  S3746

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend the vehicle and traffic law and the public officers
law, in relation to owner liability for failure of operator to comply
with traffic control indications; and providing for the repeal of such
provisions upon expiration thereof


 PURPOSE :
This bill authorizes the city of Rochester to adopt a local law that
would allow for the installation of traffic control signal photo
violation monitoring systems ("Red Light Cameras") at up to fifty
intersections throughout the city and provide for violations not to
exceed fifty dollars thereof.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :
Section 1. Amends subdivision 1 of section 235 of the VTL to make
technical changes.

Section 2. Amends section 235 of the VTL to make technical changes.

Section 3. Amends VTL section 235 to make technical changes.

Section 4. Amends subdivision 1 of section 236 of the VTL to make
technical changes.

Section 5. Amends subdivision 1 of section 236 of the VTL to authorize
the city of Rochester to adopt a local law establishing a red light
camera demonstration program at fifty intersections throughout the
county and imposing monetary fines for violations thereof. The section
further outlines the parameters for establishment of such a program as
well as penalty provisions.

Section 6. Amends subdivision 10 of section 237 of the VTL to make
technical changes.

Section 7. Amends section 237 of the VTL to add a new subdivision 10.

Section 8. Amends paragraph f of subdivision 1 of section 239 of the
VTL to define a notice of violation.

Section 9. Amends paragraph f of subdivision 1 of section 239 of the
vehicle and traffic law regarding notices of violation.

Section 10. Amends subdivisions 1 and I-a and paragraphs a and g of
subdivision 2 of section 240 of the VTL regarding technical changes to
notices of hearing.

Section 11. Amends subdivisions 1 and 1-a and paragraphs a and g of
subdivision 2 of section 240 of the VTL regarding formal notices of
hearings, contesting of fines, and records.of hearings.

Section 12. Amends subdivisions 1 and 2 of section 241 of the VTL
regarding hearing officers.  and hearings.

Section 13. Subdivisions 1 and 2 of section 241 of the VTL is amended
regarding contestation of liability.

Section 14. Paragraph a of subdivision 5-a of section 401 of the VTL
makes technical amendments to the VTL.

Section 15. Paragraph a of subdivision 5-a of section 401 of the
vehicle and traffic law is amended to prohibit the registration or
renewal of a motor vehicle if an applicant has three or more

outstanding red light camera violations under the foregoing
provisions.

Section 16. Amends the VTL to add a new section 1111 (b) to authorize
the city of Rochester to adopt a local law establishing a red light
camera demonstration program at no more than fifty intersections
throughout the city and imposing monetary fines for violations
thereof. The section further outlines the parameters for establishment
of such program as well as penalty provisions.

Section 17. The opening paragraph and paragraph (c) of subdivision 1
of section 1809 of the VTL is amended to make technical changes.

Section 18. Subdivision 1 of section 1809 of the VTL is amended to
make technical changes.

Section 19. Paragraph a of subdivision 1 of section 1809-e of the VTL
is amended to make technical changes.

Section 20. Subdivision 2 of section 87 of the public officers law is
amended by adding a new paragraph k to include photographs,
microphotographs, videotape or other recorded images prepared under
authority of section 1111 (b) of the VTL.

Section 21. Makes the purchase or lease of equipment for establishment
of red light camera programs subject to section 103 of the general
municipal law.

Section 22. Establishes the effective date and sunset of such program.

 EXISTING LAW :
New York city is currently the only municipality authorized to have a
demonstration program utilizing red light cameras.

 JUSTIFICATION :
In 1988 the New York State legislature enacted legislation that
allowed New York city to establish a demonstration program to install
photo monitoring devices to record vehicles going through red light
signals at traffic intersections. "Red Light Camera Programs" have
proven to be an effective traffic safety measure that prevent injuries
and the loss of life due to accidents caused by red light running.

Since its inception in December of 1993, hundreds of thousands of
vehicles, including buses and taxicabs, have been caught going through
red lights by the traffic control monitoring devices in New York city.
In calendar year 2005 alone, 306,117 violations or Notices of
Liability ("NOLs") were issued to Violators.

A large number of traffic accidents resulting in bodily injury and
death to motorists, passengers, pedestrians and bicyclists are due to
the failure of motorists to obey traffic control signals located at
intersections. "Right angle" and pedestrian accidents attributed to
red light running are among the leading causes of traffic fatalities.
By reducing the number of vehicles running red lights, the likelihood
of "right angle" and pedestrian type accidents is reduced. The
extended use of these devices has been shown to dramatically reduce
the number of violations at the intersections being monitored.

Red Light Camera Programs have proven to be an effective traffic
safety initiative whose success has been recognized by the State
Legislature and the New York City Council in their repeated
authorizations to extend the initial demonstration program. This
legislation would authorize the city of Rochester to follow New York
city's lead by allowing its city council to establish such a
demonstration program to further promote safety and decrease motor
vehicle accidents.
 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
None.

 LOCAL FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
This bill will increase revenue for the city of Rochester through the
placement of red light cameras at intersections throughout the city
should a local law be adopted to establish such a program.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect on the thirtieth day after it shall have
become a law and shall expire on December 1, 2014.
